eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent high pressure and strong late-summer insolation are positioning Houston for a daily maximum near the upper 90s to low 100s on August 26, 2026.** Official National Weather Service forecasts from the Houston/Galveston office call for highs around 100–102 °F under mostly sunny skies, light southwest winds, and low rain chances (around 20 %), with a Heat Advisory in effect through evening due to heat indices reaching 107–112 °F. Observations at key stations like Hobby Airport have already hit the upper 90s by mid-afternoon, consistent with model runs showing continued subsidence suppressing cloud development and allowing efficient surface heating.

The market’s heavy weighting toward 98–99 °F (87.5 % implied probability) reflects trader assessment that the official maximum—likely measured at a primary airport station—will fall just short of 100 °F amid slight model variability and any late-day mixing. Higher bins (100–101 °F at 11 %, 102–103 °F at 1 %) remain possible if peak heating aligns with the warmer forecast solutions, but current consensus data and the low likelihood of significant cloud cover or precipitation today keep those outcomes secondary. Upcoming evening observations and the final NWS verification will resolve the market.

Model consensus and recent observations show the marine layer remaining shallow but persistent enough to limit peak heating, with any breaks in clouds offering only modest upside risk. eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models for August 27 point to a high near 23–25°C in Mexico City, driven by the city’s 2,240-meter elevation and ongoing rainy-season cloud cover that limits daytime heating.** Scattered showers and partly cloudy skies, consistent with patterns observed on August 26, are expected to cap afternoon temperatures and align with climatological averages around 23°C for late August. Trader emphasis on 24–25°C outcomes reflects this consensus while acknowledging uncertainty from variable precipitation timing and model spread. Lower probabilities for 26°C or above stem from the moderating effects of typical monsoon moisture, and cooler readings remain possible only with earlier or heavier rain. Updated model runs ahead of the peak heating window will refine these market-implied odds.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the Met Office and European centers indicate London’s August 28 maximum will likely reach 22–25 °C under southwesterly flow following Thursday’s thunderstorms. Persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and stronger winds (15–25 km/h) are expected to limit surface heating and prevent the higher readings that would require clear skies and lighter winds. Ensemble spreads show modest uncertainty tied to exact shower timing and Atlantic moisture, keeping 23 °C and 24 °C as the closest outcomes in trader pricing while capping the chance of 25 °C or above. Updated runs and observed trends through Friday morning will refine these probabilities ahead of market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon conditions, reinforced by the recent passage of Typhoon Obet outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility, are driving extensive cloud cover, scattered to widespread thunderstorms, and reduced solar insolation across Metro Manila ahead of August 28. Official PAGASA guidance and ensemble forecasts emphasize moderate to heavy rainfall with southwest winds, which limits daytime heating and keeps maximum temperatures clustered near the long-term August average of roughly 30–31 °C but frequently capped lower. This meteorological setup produces tight model spreads centered on 28–30 °C, aligning with the closely matched market-implied probabilities for 29 °C and 30 °C. Minor variations in convective timing or brief clearing could nudge the daily high across those thresholds, while stronger monsoon surges would favor outcomes at or below 28 °C. Updated model runs and PAGASA bulletins through Friday will refine the exact maximum.
